_description: Per-leaf merge-strategy registry consumed by hooks/lib/overlay-master-mutate.sh. Default deep-merge semantics (jq `*` operator: recursive object merge; arrays replaced) preserve adopter-override-wins semantics at the entity level. Declared UNION leaves are the explicit exception: foundation declares the list-typed shape; adopter extends rather than shadows. Per-leaf UNION at these paths produces concat+dedup (`(existing + payload) | unique`) at write time.
_design_rationale: Two leaves are conceptually SETS, not maps: dimension_prefixes (allowed tag-prefix slugs) and user_facing_dimensions (subset elevated for cap-25 audit). Foundation lists these as arrays; adopter overlay declares additional members rather than replacing the foundation list. Without UNION semantics, the only way an adopter can preserve foundation members while adding new ones is to repeat the foundation set verbatim in their overlay — fragile and silently breaks on foundation upgrades that touch the list. UNION matches `_adopter_extension_path` notation `overlay-master.tagging.taxonomy.dimension_prefixes[]` already documented in tagging-rules.json.

entity_identity_keys._description: R-52 array-entry identity, rule-first (governance/_index.json R-52 rule_text + operation_set are the SoT; this block is the per-slot declaration the collision walk in hooks/lib/foundation-overlay-load.sh reads — never a hardcoded field name in the walk). For each array-of-object entity slot in the collision domain, the declared key is what makes two entries THE SAME ENTITY — unique within each side's array (foundation authoring contract; adopter obligation). Walk semantics per the rule: identity unmatched = ADD; matched with differing value (compared with _override_reason removed) = per-entry SUPERSEDE owing _override_reason on the entry; matched and value-identical = benign restatement; foundation identity omitted from the overlay array = attempted removal (DENY naming the identity). An array-of-object slot with NO entry here is FAIL-CLOSED: an overlay array over a non-empty non-union foundation array DENIES at the slot, naming the missing declaration. Scalar-value array leaves (enum/config lists such as plans.lifecycle.status_enum) have NO entity identity by ruling and never appear here — they keep whole-leaf collision semantics.

underscore_entities._description: R-52 underscore-entity allowlist — the naming-contract discriminator, declared per slot path (top-level-arm slots use the bare pillar name). MECHANISM CHOICE, recorded by the builder here: explicit per-slot allowlist over a global naming convention — a convention would force renaming shipped metadata keys, and value-type cannot be the contract (metadata can be object-shaped, e.g. frontmatter.path_routing._rule_shape_contract). Keys listed here are REAL ENTITIES despite the leading underscore; the collision walk admits them past its metadata filter, so superseding one owes _override_reason like any entity, and a null-valued overlay entry at one is rejected like any entity. Every other underscore key stays metadata (filtered).

_operation_set: ADD + SUPERSEDE only — there is no NULLIFY. An adopter overlay may ADD a key foundation does not declare, or SUPERSEDE a key foundation does declare with a FULL replacement value carrying per-entry `_override_reason` (R-52). It may not delete a foundation entry from the merged view: foundation conventions are immutable-by-design for adopters. A `null` overlay value is NOT a delete — the merge primitive (jq `*`) has no delete, so a null merges as a KEY WITH NO CONTRACT (still present in `keys[]`, hence still accepted, while every required[]/tier read under it yields nothing) — strictly worse than not attempting the override. hooks/lib/foundation-overlay-load.sh therefore REJECTS null-valued overlay entity entries before the merge (loud stderr finding naming each path; the foundation entry stands), and hooks/pre-write-guard.sh independently filters null-contract types out of the union accepted-type set. To make a foundation convention stop firing, SUPERSEDE it with a permissive replacement and say why in `_override_reason`; retiring a foundation convention outright is a maintainer-side source edit, not an adopter operation. Array-of-object entity slots follow the R-52 ARRAY-ENTRY IDENTITY contract: entries match on the entity_identity_keys-declared key — unmatched = ADD, matched-and-differing = per-entry SUPERSEDE (reason on the entry), matched-and-identical = restatement, omitted foundation identity = attempted removal (DENY).
_shape_handling: When a declared UNION leaf has dict-shape on either side (legacy/test fixture), the library falls back to object-recursive-merge for that leaf (preserves baseline test shape). Mixed shape (array on one side, dict on other) resolves to payload-wins. The library does not coerce shape; producers (skills) are responsible for emitting the declared shape per leaf.
